abstract: Hack-Verifiable TextArena embeds exploitable reward-hacking opportunities directly into environments to automatically and reliably measure reward hacking at scale.

title: Auditing Games for Sandbagging
abstract: Red-team/blue-team auditing game where red teams create conditionally-underperforming (sandbagging) models and blue teams attempt detection with black-box, internals, and training-based methods — with limited success, evidencing a hard-to-detect evaluation-gaming risk.

title: SafeAgentBench: A Benchmark for Safe Task Planning of Embodied LLM Agents
abstract: Benchmark + SafeAgentEnv simulator for hazard-aware task planning of embodied LLM agents; measures whether agents recognize and refuse physically hazardous tasks in interactive 3D environments.

title: LabSafety Bench: Benchmarking LLMs on Safety Issues in Scientific Labs
abstract: OSHA-grounded benchmark evaluating LLMs/VLMs on laboratory safety; models make critical lab-safety errors despite high general performance — a physical-safety hazard for AI lab assistants.

title: MHSafeEval: Role-Aware Interaction-Level Evaluation of Mental Health Safety in Large Language Models
abstract: Role-aware safety taxonomy + agent-based, trajectory-level adversarial multi-turn evaluation of LLM mental-health counseling; reveals cumulative safety failures that static single-turn benchmarks miss.

title: LoRA-as-an-Attack! Piercing LLM Safety Under The Share-and-Play Scenario
abstract: Injects a backdoor into a LoRA adapter and propagates it through the share-and-play adapter ecosystem; studies merging a backdoored LoRA with benign adapters and the resulting safety compromise.

title: Attack via Overfitting: 10-shot Benign Fine-tuning to Jailbreak LLMs
abstract: Fine-tuning on as few as 10 benign QA pairs causes an aligned LLM to overfit and forget refusal behavior, jailbreaking it while evading moderation models.

title: Why LLM Safety Guardrails Collapse After Fine-tuning: A Similarity Analysis Between Alignment and Fine-tuning Datasets
abstract: Shows high representation similarity between upstream alignment data and the downstream fine-tuning task weakens safety guardrails, explaining and predicting fine-tuning-based de-alignment.

title: Backdoor Activation Attack: Attack Large Language Models using Activation Steering for Safety-Alignment
abstract: Uses contrastive activation steering vectors at inference to flip safety-relevant behavior (toxicity, harmfulness) of instruction-tuned LLMs without optimization or weight updates.

title: Refusal Direction is Universal Across Safety-Aligned Languages
abstract: Shows a single 'refusal direction' in activation space governs refusal across languages; ablating it cross-lingually bypasses safety, generalizing refusal-direction-ablation jailbreaks.

title: JULI: Jailbreak Large Language Models by Self-Introspection
abstract: Manipulates exposed token log-probabilities via a small BiasNet to jailbreak API-accessible LLMs without access to weights or the generation process.

title: Implicit Jailbreak Attacks via Cross-Modal Information Concealment on Vision-Language Models
abstract: Embeds malicious instructions into images via LSB steganography plus adversarial suffixes so a VLM reconstructs and executes them across modalities, achieving high ASR on commercial MLLMs.

title: Exploring Typographic Visual Prompts Injection Threats in Cross-Modality Generation Models
abstract: Typographic Visual Prompt Injection (TVPI): rendering attacker instructions as text inside an image hijacks LVLM perception and image-to-image generation.

title: Watermark Stealing in Large Language Models
abstract: By querying a watermarked LLM's API, an attacker reverse-engineers the scheme, enabling both scrubbing (removing the watermark) and spoofing (forging it onto attacker text).

title: Text Embeddings Reveal (Almost) As Much As Text
abstract: Iterative 'vec2text' inversion reconstructs most of the original text (including PII) from dense embeddings, showing embedding stores in RAG/vector DBs leak their source text.

title: GASLITEing the Retrieval: Exploring Vulnerabilities in Dense Embedding-based Search
abstract: GASLITE gradient-crafts adversarial passages tuned to embedding-space geometry so they are retrieved for whole query distributions, hijacking RAG retrieval at the embedding/retriever level.

title: VectorSmuggle: Steganographic Exfiltration in Embedding Stores and a Cryptographic Provenance Defense
abstract: Hides exfiltrated data inside RAG vector-store embeddings via retrieval-preserving rotations (orthogonal/Givens) that evade anomaly detection; proposes a cryptographic-provenance defense.

title: Low-Resource Languages Jailbreak GPT-4
abstract: Translating an unsafe request into a low-resource language bypasses GPT-4 guardrails; translating the answer back recovers the harmful content — a cross-lingual translation jailbreak.

title: H-CoT: Hijacking the Chain-of-Thought Safety Reasoning Mechanism to Jailbreak Large Reasoning Models, Including OpenAI o1/o3, DeepSeek-R1, and Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking
abstract: Injects fabricated benign chain-of-thought into the reasoning trace of large reasoning models to hijack their safety-reasoning step, collapsing refusal rates on o1/o3, DeepSeek-R1, Gemini Flash Thinking.

title: Exploiting LLM Quantization
abstract: Crafts a model benign in full precision but malicious (vulnerable-code-gen, content injection, over-refusal) once a victim applies standard quantization — a quantization-conditioned backdoor distributed via model hubs.

title: Architectural Backdoors for Within-Batch Data Stealing and Model Inference Manipulation
abstract: A backdoor planted in the network architecture (not weights) exploits batched inference to leak one user's inputs to another in the same batch and manipulate other users' outputs.

title: Breaking Minds, Breaking Systems: Jailbreaking Large Language Models via Human-like Psychological Manipulation
abstract: Applies human psychological-manipulation tactics (authority, reciprocity, sustained pressure, anthropomorphic consistency) over a dialogue to corrupt LLM policy adherence, achieving high ASR while bypassing defenses.

title: Jailbreaking to Jailbreak (J2)
abstract: A human red-teamer seeds a refusal-trained LLM to overcome its own refusals (J1), turning it into a red-teaming agent (J2) that then jailbreaks other models AND itself across multi-turn conversations, learning from prior attempts in-context. Shows aligned models can be repurposed as scalable attackers.

title: X-Teaming: Multi-Turn Jailbreaks and Defenses with Adaptive Multi-Agents
abstract: X-Teaming is an adaptive multi-agent framework for multi-turn jailbreaks using four collaborating roles - Planner, Attacker, Verifier, Optimizer - that iteratively plan, execute, judge and refine attack trajectories. Releases XGuard-Train, an open multi-turn safety-training dataset for defense.

title: AgenticRed: Evolving Agentic Systems for Red-Teaming
abstract: AgenticRed treats red-teaming as an open-ended SYSTEM-DESIGN problem: each generation an LLM programs a new agentic attacker system drawing on an ever-growing archive of prior discoveries (with FailedPromptMemory / SucceedPromptMemory), self-improving without human intervention. Reaches 96-100% ASR on open-weight models and 100% on GPT-5.1/DeepSeek-R1/V3.2, with strong transfer.

title: AUTORISE: Agent-Driven Strategy Evolution for Red-Teaming Large Language Models
authors: ^[ambiguous] author list not confirmed from search snippets
abstract: AUTORISE uses an agent that evolves red-teaming STRATEGIES (not just prompts) over iterations, growing a library of reusable attack strategies that generalize across targets - an agent-driven, self-improving strategy-evolution paradigm.

title: Redefining AI Red Teaming in the Agentic Era: From Weeks to Hours
abstract: An agentic red-teaming system (Dreadnode SDK) where operators specify goals in natural language via a TUI and the agent orchestrates attack selection, transform composition, execution and reporting across 45+ attacks, 450+ transforms, 130+ scorers, supporting multi-agent/multilingual/multimodal targets. 85% ASR on Llama Scout with zero human-written code; compresses testing cycles from weeks to hours.

title: RADAR: A Risk-Aware Dynamic Multi-Agent Framework for LLM Safety Evaluation via Role-Specialized Collaboration
authors: ^[ambiguous] author list not confirmed from search snippets
abstract: RADAR is a risk-aware dynamic multi-agent safety-evaluation framework where role-specialized agents collaborate to probe LLMs, dynamically allocating effort to higher-risk regions of the behavior space.

title: Jailbreak-R1: Exploring the Jailbreak Capabilities of LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
authors: ^[ambiguous] author list not confirmed from search snippets
abstract: Jailbreak-R1 trains an attacker LLM with a three-stage RL curriculum - Cold Start (SFT), Warm-up Exploration (diversity + consistency rewards), and Enhanced Jailbreak (progressive jailbreak rewards) - to generate effective AND diverse attack prompts, explicitly balancing ASR against attack diversity.

title: Chasing Moving Targets with Online Self-Play Reinforcement Learning for Safer Language Models
authors: ^[ambiguous] author list not confirmed from search snippets
abstract: Co-trains attacker and defender via ONLINE self-play RL so the safety target keeps moving: the defender hardens against an attacker that continuously adapts, closing the gap that static red-team datasets leave behind. A self-play continuous-hardening paradigm.

title: CoP: Agentic Red-teaming for Large Language Models using Composition of Principles
authors: ^[ambiguous] author list not confirmed from search snippets
abstract: CoP frames agentic red-teaming as the COMPOSITION of human-provided red-teaming principles: an agent composes and chains atomic jailbreak principles into novel multi-step attacks, blending human strategic priors with automated search.

title: Quality-Diversity Red-Teaming: Automated Generation of High-Quality and Diverse Attackers for LLMs
authors: ^[ambiguous] author list not confirmed from search snippets
abstract: QDRT combines behavior-conditioned attacker training, a behavior-assignment strategy and a MAP-Elites buffer to jointly optimize attack quality and diversity, reporting +22.13% QD-Score and +19.33% behavior coverage over prior QD red-teaming. A learning-based successor to Rainbow Teaming's pure evolutionary search.

title: Quality-Diversity Evolution for Discovering Diverse Vulnerabilities in LLM Safety
abstract: A MAP-Elites framework that evolves INTERPRETABLE semantic-level attack strategies (not token-level gibberish) across behavioral dimensions strategy-type x encoding-method x prompt-length, exposing systematic model-specific weakness profiles (e.g. GPT-4o-mini -> hypothetical+ROT13; Claude 3.5 uniformly robust).

title: Cross-Generational Transfer of Adversarial Attacks Reveals Non-Monotonic Safety Alignment in LLMs
authors: ^[ambiguous] author list not confirmed from search snippets
abstract: Uses MAP-Elites QD search to discover diverse jailbreaks across seven harm categories, then builds a model-generation transfer matrix by replaying attacks across model generations - showing safety alignment is NON-MONOTONIC (newer models can regress on vulnerabilities older ones fixed). A regression-tracking red-team method.

title: A Coin Flip for Safety: LLM Judges Fail to Reliably Measure Adversarial Robustness
abstract: Shows single LLM judges measuring jailbreak ASR exhibit high variance, low inter-judge agreement and poor calibration - near coin-flip on borderline cases. Recommends multi-judge ensembles + human anchoring as calibration ground truth. A direct reliability critique of the llm-as-a-judge paradigm.

title: When Scanners Lie: Evaluator Instability in LLM Red-Teaming
authors: ^[ambiguous] author list not confirmed from search snippets
abstract: Demonstrates that automated red-team scanners/evaluators (garak-style probe scorers, judge models) give unstable verdicts on identical transcripts, so reported vulnerability counts depend heavily on evaluator choice. Argues for evaluator-stability reporting and consensus scoring.

title: ADVERSA: Measuring Multi-Turn Guardrail Degradation and Judge Reliability in Large Language Models
authors: ^[ambiguous] author list not confirmed from search snippets
abstract: ADVERSA adds per-round structured scoring, trajectory logging and MULTI-JUDGE CONSENSUS to multi-turn red-teaming, quantifying how guardrails degrade turn-by-turn and how judge reliability varies across conversation depth.

title: MultiBreak: A Scalable and Diverse Multi-turn Jailbreak Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Safety
authors: ^[ambiguous] author list not confirmed from search snippets
abstract: MultiBreak is a scalable, diverse multi-turn jailbreak benchmark with LLaMA-Guard and GPT-4o-mini judges, designed to evaluate LLM safety against conversational (not single-shot) attacks at scale.

title: MCPSecBench: A Systematic Security Benchmark and Playground for Testing Model Context Protocols
abstract: MCPSecBench is a systematic MCP security benchmark + playground covering tool poisoning, prompt injection, DNS rebinding, RCE and elicitation attacks across major MCP platforms (Claude, OpenAI and others), revealing platform-specific gaps in static validation and context isolation.

title: PISmith: Reinforcement Learning-based Red Teaming for Prompt Injection Defenses
authors: ^[ambiguous] author list not confirmed from search snippets
abstract: PISmith trains an attacker LLM with RL to optimize INJECTED prompts in a black-box setting, systematically stress-testing prompt-injection DEFENSES (guardrails/classifiers) rather than base models - RL red-teaming aimed at the defender layer.

title: Reverse Constitutional AI: Controllable Toxic Data Generation via Probability-Clamped RLAIF
authors: ^[ambiguous] author list not confirmed from search snippets
abstract: Reverse Constitutional AI (R-CAI) inverts a written constitution to AUTOMATICALLY generate red-team data and systematically evaluate aligned models, using probability-clamped RLAIF for controllable toxic-data generation. Operationalizes constitutional-AI as a teaming method (constitution -> adversarial probes).

title: NRT-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-Turn Red-Teaming of LLM Operator Agents in Safety-Critical Control Rooms
authors: ^[ambiguous] author list not confirmed from search snippets
abstract: NRT-Bench red-teams a five-role LLM operator team running a simulated nuclear power-plant control room governed by six critical safety functions; adversaries inject over four channels in bounded multi-turn sessions, and harm is an OBJECTIVE physical signal rather than LLM-judged text - sidestepping judge unreliability.

title: Beyond Benchmarks: Dynamic, Automatic and Systematic Red-Teaming Agents for Trustworthy Medical Language Models
authors: ^[ambiguous] author list not confirmed from search snippets
abstract: A dynamic automated red-teaming AGENT for medical LLMs whose LLM-judge is calibrated against board-certified clinicians, achieving high inter-rater reliability - a sector-specific (medical) human-anchored judge protocol.

title: T-MAP: Red-Teaming LLM Agents with Trajectory-aware Evolutionary Search
authors: ^[ambiguous] author list not confirmed from search snippets
abstract: T-MAP evolves whole agent TRAJECTORIES (tool-call sequences), not single prompts, using trajectory-aware evolutionary search to red-team tool-using agents - extending QD/evolutionary red-teaming from text to multi-step agent behavior.

title: The Promise and Peril of Artificial Intelligence - Violet Teaming Offers a Balanced Path Forward
abstract: Position paper proposing 'violet teaming' as an integrative approach that combines red-team risk identification with blue-team solution-building and embeds social-benefit/responsibility considerations directly into system design - a proactive, responsible-by-design alternative to reactive red teaming.

title: 2026 Cybersecurity Predictions - AI Red Teaming via Crowdsourced Bug Bounty
abstract: Industry predictions describing the maturation of crowdsourced AI red teaming via bug-bounty platforms, with human crowds incentivized to find jailbreaks and safety failures alongside automated attackers.

title: Constitutional Classifiers: Defending against Universal Jailbreaks across Thousands of Hours of Red Teaming
abstract: Anthropic trains constitutional classifiers against universal jailbreaks, validated through thousands of hours of human red teaming delivered via an external HackerOne bug-bounty program - concrete deployment of crowdsourced red teaming + a constitutional (llm-as-a-defender) control.

title: FragFuse: Bypassing Access Control of Large Language Model Agents via Memory-Based Query Fragmentation and Fusion
org: University of Georgia / University of Chicago / University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
abstract: FragFuse is the first attack that bypasses LLM-agent access control by fragmenting a prohibited query, writing the fragments into the agent's long-term memory in benign form via a 'carrier query', then retrieving and fusing them at execution time via an optimized fusion instruction. Exploits a 'temporal channel': the malicious intent never appears explicitly in the final user query. Black-box, ordinary-user threat model. Achieves average 86.3% bypass success rate (BSR) and 41.1% end-to-end harmful-task success across RAP/SeeAct/OSAgent/InspAgent vs 3 SOTA access-control mechanisms (GuardAgent, AGrail, ShieldAgent), with only 4.4% avg task-success degradation; defeats prompt-injection and perplexity detectors.

title: Security Engineering of OpenClaw: Analyzing Attack Surface Expansion and Trust-Boundary Violations
abstract: Structural security analysis of OpenClaw, a self-hosted execution-coupled multi-agent LLM system where semantic outputs map directly to executable primitives (shell, files, network, skills). Introduces quantitative metrics for compromise amplification, cumulative boundary instability (CBI), privilege drift, attack-surface entropy, and escalation curvature. With one agent, compromise probability is 0.24; with seven agents under a permissive 'any-agent' aggregation rule, it rises to 0.86 (3.58x amplification). Prompt injection raises attack-surface entropy 0.42->0.71 and mean privilege drift 0.03->0.21, with positive escalation curvature (0.08). Defensive controls (policy gating, execution filtering) cut compromise/boundary-failure/privilege-drift by 0.10/0.10/0.02 (all p<0.0001), at the cost of task utility (0.93->0.89) and latency (420->468 ms).

title: MAStrike: Shapley-Guided Collusive Red-Teaming on Multi-Agent Systems
org: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign / Virtue AI / University of Chicago
abstract: MAStrike is a closed-loop framework for collusive red-teaming of hierarchical multi-agent systems (MAS). It proposes the first agent-level Shapley value analysis for MAS — quantifying each agent's marginal contribution to system robustness using attack success rate (ASR) as a coalition value function, plus a pairwise Shapley interaction index. A Shapley-guided red-team agent then selects synergy-aware coalitions and generates coordinated, role-aware adversarial injections, iteratively refined via structured failure diagnosis. Introduces MABench (finance, software-engineering, CRM hierarchical MAS). Achieves 61.8% ASR on Claude Opus 4.7 and 55.6% on GPT-5.5 (compromise budget k=2), vs near-zero for prior single-agent/template baselines (TAMAS, GCA, AutoTransform, AiTM). Shows enterprise guardrails detect single-agent signals but miss distributed collusion.

title: Securing Multi-Agent GIS Systems: Risk Evaluation and Prompt Hardening Optimization
org: University of Waterloo / University of Calgary
abstract: Security-oriented framework for risk identification, evaluation, and mitigation in a commercial multi-agent conversational GIS (geospatial) system. Reproduces the commercial architecture (conversational assistant + geospatial recommender + helper agents) in a LangGraph state machine, red-teams it with an adaptive attacker LLM and deterministic binary judge over multi-turn (<=3 turn) attacks across 8 adversarial personas in 3 categories (Security, Topic/Identity, Recommender-Integrity), and hardens it via DSPy prompt optimization treating prompts as structured signatures with adversarial few-shot demonstrations. SEC attacks (credential/system-prompt extraction) are at 0% ceiling with good baseline prompts. DSPy reduces out-of-scope attacker success 84->55% and competitor-probing 87->73%, but vague-location attacks stay high because the recommender agent lacks a chain-of-thought layer (a routing-level, not prompt-level, vulnerability).

title: From Shield to Target: Denial-of-Service Attacks on LLM-Based Agent Guardrails
org: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology / Zhejiang University of Technology
abstract: Reveals 'reasoning-extension DoS', a new vulnerability class in LLM-based agent guardrails: because guardrails follow a structured analytical schema (enumerate risk categories, assess evidence, produce a verdict), adversarial content shaped like the guardrail's own schema traps it in unbounded reasoning loops, inflating per-call compute 13-63x (up to 148x latency). A beam-search optimizer (LLM-as-Proposer with a strategy bank, or a mechanism-aware structural mutator) crafts fluent natural-language payloads on a single open-source surrogate (TS-Guard-8B) that transfer to 8 guardrail backbones. Demonstrated end-to-end on OpenHands (code), LangGraph (multi-agent), BrowserGym (web), OSWorld (desktop) with up to 148x latency amplification and systemic head-of-line blocking that starves co-located agents sharing the guardrail. A single poisoned document persists as a long-lived trigger; mitigations (pre-inference filters, token budgets) only shift the failure mode (fail-open bypass vs fail-closed denial).

title: Measuring the Residual Jailbreak Surface of Frontier Large Language Models: A red-team study of Anthropic Fable 5 & Opus 4.8 models
org: AI4I — Italian Institute of Artificial Intelligence (AI Security Lab)
abstract: Automated red-team campaign on two Anthropic frontier models (Opus 4.8, Fable 5) across 7,826 harmful intents (10 categories, 55 subcategories) and four attack families (TAP, PAIR, PAP, h4rm3l) using the HackAgent framework. Every apparent success was re-adjudicated by an independent 3-judge panel (majority vote: Qwen3.7 Max, Gemini 3.5 Flash, GPT 5.5). Adaptive tree-of-attacks breaks Opus 4.8 on 11.5% of intents (6.1% Fable 5); static obfuscation is near-fully neutralised (<=0.2%). Models produced 1,620 (Opus) and 702 (Fable) panel-confirmed harmful completions spanning every harm category, found automatically, cheaply, and early.

title: Transferable Self-Evolving Playbooks for Agentic Security Auditing
org: University of Sydney / University of Warwick / UC Berkeley RDI
abstract: EVOHUNT instantiates a playbook-evolution environment for agentic vulnerability discovery: three agents (audit/discovery, evaluator, reviser) drive a loop that, starting from an EMPTY unconstrained playbook, freely adds/removes workflows, heuristics, and vulnerability knowledge based on failure analysis, with the underlying LLM and harness held fixed. Evaluated on 813 OSS GitHub advisories (training) + 371 held-out (testing). Evolution lifts Codex/GPT5.4-xhigh end-to-end exploits 6x (1.1%->6.2%); evolved OpenCode/GLM5.1 playbook surpasses OpenAI Codex Security on every metric (11.3% vs 9.2% match). Teacher->student transfer lifts Qwen students (27B 2.4%->6.5%; A3B 1.1%->4.6%). Produced 28 confirmed disclosures + a $1,500 bounty.

title: AutoDojo: Adaptive Attacks Expose Superficial Defenses and User-Underspecification Limits in LLM Agents
org: Washington University in St. Louis / Texas A&M / Johns Hopkins
abstract: AutoDojo extends AgentDojo to turn any indirect-prompt-injection (IPI) attack into a cheap black-box ADAPTIVE one against a defended agent, using a small offline optimizer LLM (Gemini 3.1 Pro), a leaderboard of candidates, and only the binary ASR success signal (no weights/gradients, budget of 6 iterations). Across 9 SOTA IPI defenses x 5 target models x 3 task suites (banking/slack/travel), adaptive optimization raises ASR well above static-injection levels: against a filter that drives static ASR to 0%, AutoDojo recovers 28% overall and 64% on action-open tasks. Also exposes a structural limit — ASR is much higher on under-specified (action-open) tasks where the user delegates the action to attacker-controlled content.

title: SkillMutator: Benchmarking and Defending Language-and-Code Cross-modal Attacks on LLM Agent Skills
abstract: SkillMutator is the first benchmark for install-time detection of language-and-code CROSS-MODAL attacks on LLM Agent Skills (composite artifacts pairing a natural-language SKILL.md with executable scripts/resources). An adaptive attacker mutates benign skills across 13 attack categories (4 threat groups) via 4-stage analysis + iterative scanner-evasion refinement, yielding 187 mutated scenarios where unsafe behavior emerges from the interaction of SKILL.md directives and helper code. Existing scanners detect only 2%-8% (open-source), 9%-17% (commercial). A 4-phase reasoning-trajectory distillation framework lifts a local Qwen2.5-Coder-7B scanner from 17.1% to 88.2% detection, exceeding frontier GPT-5.4 (86.8%) without third-party content exposure.

title: FinRED: An Expert-Guided Benchmark Generation and Evaluation Framework for Financial LLM Red-Teaming
org: DATUMO INC. / KAIST / Financial Security Institute (FSI), Republic of Korea
abstract: FinRED is an expert-guided red-teaming construction+evaluation framework for financial LLM safety. It uses a two-level financial risk taxonomy (5 Level-1 categories / 26 Level-2 subtypes) mapping global standards (FATF, EU DORA, ISO/IEC 27001, BIS/BCBS, NIST, OWASP) to threats from regulatory evasion to complex fraud, plus a schema-driven pipeline converting ~500 real financial/regulatory documents into context-grounded Behavioral Prompt seeds (5,805 expert-validated seeds). A finance-specific 5-dimension judge rubric (harmfulness/persuasiveness/refusal-quality/factualness/evasiveness) aligns better with 12 FSI experts than static rubrics (human-LLM agreement 76.92%->88.46%, critical false negatives cut 28->12). Deployed in South Korea's FSI regulatory sandbox.

title: An Evaluation of Data Leakage Risks in Tool-Using LLM Agents in Realistic Scenarios
org: Korea AI Safety Institute / Singapore AI Safety Institute
abstract: Joint SG AISI / KR AISI evaluation of agent data leakage across 12 realistic non-adversarial tasks (HR, DevOps, customer support, web automation, productivity), covering 5 risk types: data awareness, audience awareness, policy compliance, data minimization, access-boundary awareness. Using ReAct scaffolds, MCP tool environments, LLM-simulated users and task-specific LLM-judge rubrics over 3 agent models x 10 runs/scenario, none achieved fully correct AND fully safe execution. Operational leakage in benign workflows is a first-order safety concern distinct from adversarial exfiltration; capability and data-handling safety must be evaluated separately.

title: Who Pays the Price? Stakeholder-Centric Prompt Injection Benchmarking for Real-world Web Agents
org: Nanyang Technological University / ST Engineering / IBM Research / UIUC
abstract: StakeBench is a stakeholder-centric prompt-injection benchmark for LLM web agents that attributes harm to the affected entity (User, third-party Seller, Platform) rather than the attack surface. 12 attack objectives realized by 22 templates (9 DPI, 13 IPI) across 12 product categories = 264 executable cases on OneStopMarket/VisualWebArena. Evaluated on NanoBrowser and BrowserUse with GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5-Flash backbones (3,168 attacked runs), measured along ASR, Task Deviation Rate (TDR), Behavioral Irregularity Rate (BIR). IPI ASR 41.67-68.16%. Failures split into Stealthy Parasitism, Misaligned Disruption, Compounded Failure regimes; vulnerability profiles diverge by stakeholder.

title: FreoStream: Enhancing Stream Guardrails via Future-Aware Reasoning and Safety-Aligned Optimization
org: South China University of Technology / BUAA
abstract: FreoStream is a streaming (token-level) LLM guardrail framework addressing two failure modes of stream guardrails: over-refusal of sensitive-but-benign tokens and safety degradation against implicit jailbreaks under incomplete context. It fine-tunes a LoRA reasoning adapter for Future-Reason-Judge (predict future, reason over full context, judge) triggered when the base guardrail flags an unsafe token, and a Safety-Aligned Optimization module that decomposes reasoning gradients to keep only the safety-aligned component. On Qwen3Guard-Stream-0.6B backbone it lowers both Over-Refusal Rate (ORR) and Attack Success Rate (ASR) vs baselines including Qwen-Stream-8B.

title: The Gate Is Only as Honest as Its Contracts: ContractGuard for the Contract Layer of Risk-Aware Causal Gating
abstract: Analyzes Risk-Aware Causal Gating (RACG), which defends tool-using LLM agents against indirect prompt injection by removing dangerous tools from the visible action space. Shows the structural guarantee relocates trust into the integrity of tool contracts (declared preconditions R_i, effects E_i, risk rho_i, authorization alpha_i). RACG contains two gates (causal + admissibility); effect integrity (E_i+R_i causal routing), not the risk label, is the load-bearing assumption. Introduces ContractGuard, a verifier with signed provenance, typed contract attestation, and runtime effect verification forming a strict necessity ladder restoring injection success to zero (L3) across an exhaustive white-box adaptive attacker and six hosted frontier models (Claude Opus 4.8/Sonnet 4.6/Haiku 4.5, Amazon Nova Premier/Nova 2 Lite, GPT-OSS-120B).

title: A Layered Security Framework Against Prompt Injection in RAG-Based Chatbots
abstract: A three-layer model-agnostic middleware defense against direct and indirect prompt injection in RAG chatbots: Layer 1 input screening (rule pattern library + fine-tuned semantic anomaly classifier), Layer 2 provenance-based instruction hierarchy at context assembly (operator/retrieval/user privilege tiers), Layer 3 output auditing (policy rule engine + semantic drift detection), plus a continuous audit/retraining loop. Evaluated on 5,080 samples across GPT-4o, Llama 3, Mistral 7B against three attacker goals (Instruction Override, Data Exfiltration, Behavioral Manipulation). Reduces macro-averaged ASR from 71.4% to 11.3%, 4.8% FPR, 61.2ms median latency; layered effect exceeds sum of single layers.

title: Rapid Poison: Practical Poisoning Attacks Against the Rapid Response Framework
org: Princeton University / Anthropic / UC Berkeley / NYU / Google DeepMind
abstract: Reveals that prompt injection can infiltrate the Rapid Response (RR) jailbreak-defense pipeline (deployed in Anthropic ASL-3 safeguards) by injecting poisoned samples into the proliferation/SFT training set. Two objectives: (I) targeted false positives on harmless samples (utility degradation) and (II) concept-based backdoor (Omission Attack) causing false negatives that generalize even to jailbreaks the defender trained against. With only 1% poisoning: up to 100% FPR and up to 96% FNR. Attacker constrained to modify only positive-class (unsafe) samples, no label poisoning.

title: Automated jailbreak attack targeting multiple defense strategies (UniAttack)
org: East China Normal University / University of Southampton / Shanghai Jiao Tong University
abstract: UniAttack is a fusion-based single-turn black-box adversarial testing framework built from a defense-oriented perspective. It extracts minimal high-impact attack features from diverse existing attacks, optimizes them via a specialized attacker LLM, and composes them into flexible templates through automated refinement. Motivated by the Swiss-cheese model, it simultaneously targets input filtering, model alignment, and output detection layers in one prompt. Achieves average ASR 87.17% (64.63%-248.82% improvement over PAIR/CIPHER/DEEPINCEPTION/LLM-FUZZER baselines) across 9 LLMs at only 0.03-4.96% of baseline token cost, with 1.01-2.81 queries per success.

title: GAS-Leak-LLM: Genetic Algorithm-Based Suffix Optimization for Black-Box LLM Jailbreaking
org: University of Pavia / Cochin University of Science and Technology
abstract: GAS-Leak-LLM is a black-box jailbreak that evolves a UNIVERSAL adversarial suffix using a genetic algorithm (selection, crossover, mutation, elitism over 100 generations), requiring no gradient or model internals. Fitness = similarity(response, harmful target) - similarity(response, refusal). Two suffix types: meaningless (Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B vocabulary tokens) and meaningful (LLM-composed coherent sentences from frequent English words). Key findings: instruction fine-tuning strongly improves alignment; semantically meaningful suffixes are substantially more effective than meaningless ones; longer suffixes matter more for robust models like Llama.

title: Forced Deferral: Manipulating Routing Decisions in Multimodal LLM Cascades
abstract: Multimodal LLM (MLLM) cascades route to a strong model only when a cheap weak model is unconfident. The Forced Deferral Attack (FDA) is an adversarial image attack that lowers the weak model's confidence to force unnecessary deferral to the strong model, shifting compute cost to the provider without targeting answer correctness. FDA learns a universal border trigger by optimizing a temperature-flattened teacher-forcing KL objective that is metric-agnostic (works against any uncertainty score), semantics-preserving (border-only, central content intact), and universal across queries. Consistently increases strong-model routing across datasets/families/deferral metrics, beating image-perturbation and prompt-injection baselines, and survives JPEG/Gaussian/bit-depth preprocessing.

title: Analyzing Defensive Misdirection Against Model-Guided Automated Attacks on Agentic AI Systems
org: Keysight Technologies (Application & Threat Intelligence Research Center)
abstract: Probabilistic analysis of model-guided automated jailbreak/prompt-injection attacks that use an automated LLM judge to evaluate target responses and refine prompts. Shows conventional detect-and-block defenses let attacker ASR approach 1 as query budget grows, because predictable refusals give useful feedback to automated search. Proposes detect-and-misdirect: detected malicious interactions get controlled, plausible but non-operational misleading responses that induce false positives in the attacker's judge, bounding asymptotic ASR. A proof-of-concept, Contextual Misdirection via Progressive Engagement (CMPE), reduces estimated ASR by up to two orders of magnitude and nearly eliminates verified success in end-to-end PAIR and GPTFuzz runs.

title: Context-Fractured Decomposition Attacks on Tool-Using LLM Agents: Exploiting Artifact Provenance Gaps
org: UCLA; Texas A&M; Cisco; University of Mississippi
abstract: Tool-using LLM agents persist state in artifacts (files, logs) so jailbreak defenses must reason across cross-step composition. The paper operationalizes the 'provenance gap' for tool-using agents and introduces Context-Fractured Decomposition (CFD): cross-context multi-step jailbreaks that preserve benign-looking intermediate artifacts in an early interaction and elicit harmful behavior later, possibly in a different agent instance or workflow stage, via individually innocuous tool actions whose risk emerges only under delayed artifact-mediated composition. Across agent-system jailbreak benchmarks (AgentDojo), CFD improves attack success rates by up to 28.14 percentage points over SOTA baselines even against strong single-turn judges. Accepted at ICML 2026 Workshop on Failure Modes in Agentic AI (FAGEN).

title: Data Agents Under Attack: Vulnerabilities in LLM-Driven Analytical Systems
org: Nanyang Technological University; The Hong Kong Polytechnic University; Tsinghua University
abstract: Data agents interleave LLM-driven reasoning with relational data access, executable analytical tools, and multi-step workflow orchestration, recombining concerns of database security and LLM-agent security into failure modes neither captures alone. The paper develops a layered vulnerability framework identifying eight data-agent-specific vulnerabilities (V1-V8) across interpretation, execution, and policy layers; introduces an attack taxonomy of three adversary goals (Hijack, Mislead, Drain), seven tactics, and fourteen techniques (T1.1-T7.2) paired with an LLM payload-generation pipeline grounded in real database schemas; and evaluates these on six systems (DataInterpreter, DB-GPT, DeepAnalyze, LAMBDA, Databricks Genie, BigQuery) yielding 3,075 tests.

title: Assessing Automated Prompt Injection Attacks in Agentic Environments
abstract: Indirect prompt injection threatens LLM agents that interact with untrusted external data, yet automated attack methods proven effective for jailbreaking remain underexplored in realistic agentic settings. The paper presents an empirical evaluation of automated prompt-injection attacks against LLM agents, adapting white-box (GCG) and black-box (TAP) methods to the agentic setting within AgentDojo. Across 80 task pairs over four domains and three models (Qwen3-4B, Gemma3-4B, GPT-5), black-box TAP substantially outperforms gradient-based GCG (45.2% vs 24.1% ASR on Qwen3-4B). Task-universal attacks transfer effectively, but attacks optimized on smaller open-source models do not transfer to frontier models like GPT-5, highlighting automated prompt injection as a credible but model-dependent threat with significant barriers to model-agnostic exploitation.

title: SecureClaw: Clawing Back Control of LLM Agents
abstract: Tool-using LLM agents face two distinct security failures: unauthorized external actions and exposure of sensitive plaintext inside the runtime before any final output check can intervene. Existing defenses usually protect one boundary (planner/runtime or action sink) and so cannot secure both surfaces. SecureClaw is a dual-boundary architecture placing authorization at the effect sink (writes follow a PREVIEW->COMMIT protocol; only a trusted executor commits the exact canonical request authorized by policy) and plaintext confinement at the read boundary (sensitive reads pass through a trusted gateway returning opaque handles plus bounded summaries as an explicit declassification interface). Across AgentDojo, AgentLeak, and ASB, SecureClaw is the only evaluated common-harness baseline that simultaneously retains usable utility and achieves 0% ASR on ASB, 0.64% ASR on AgentDojo, and 3.23% overall leak on AgentLeak's attacked parity lane.

title: Toward Secure LLM Agents: Threat Surfaces, Attacks, Defenses, and Evaluation
org: Nanjing University; Technical University of Munich
abstract: A lifecycle-based, systems-oriented SoK synthesizing 247 papers (2023-Apr 2026) on LLM agent security. Models agent security around the interaction of information flow, delegated authority, and persistent state across the agentic loop, organized by four research questions (modeling, threat surfaces/attack families, defenses/tradeoffs, evaluation/benchmark gaps). Finds prompt injection and tool-mediated control-flow hijacking dominate the field while persistent state corruption and multi-agent propagation are emerging central concerns; current defenses provide useful building blocks but remain weakly compositional; existing benchmarks underrepresent long-horizon, stateful, and deployment-sensitive risks. Argues secure agents require explicit trust boundaries, principled privilege control, provenance-aware state management, and deployment-aligned evaluation.

title: PI-Hunter: Automated Red-Teaming for Exposing and Localizing Prompt Injections
org: Google Cloud AI Research; Google; Michigan State University
abstract: PI-Hunter is an automated agentic auditing framework that shifts red-teaming of LLM agents from attack-success optimization to injection-exposure: it statically maps an agent's tools/retrieval interfaces/external sources, then evolves source-aware probing test cases through feedback-driven mutation to induce the agent to retrieve, process and reveal latent malicious instructions embedded in untrusted external sources, localizing the specific source->tool ingestion path. A patch-and-reexplore loop applies transient mitigations to drive coverage toward unexplored attack surfaces. On AgentDojo and AgentDyn it substantially improves source localization, instruction exposure and ingestion-path diversity over a strong agentic baseline, and remains effective under Spotlighting, MELON and PIGuard defenses.

title: RedEdit: Agentic Red-Teaming of Image Safety Classifiers via MCTS-Guided Photo-Editing
org: HKUST (Guangzhou); Sun Yat-sen University; Weixin AI, Tencent
abstract: RedEdit is a black-box red-teaming agent that formulates user-style photo-editing evasion of image safety classifiers as a combinatorial search over edit-tool sequences. A VLM-based proposer supplies domain-aware candidate edits and a Monte-Carlo Tree Search planner prioritizes promising edit paths while backtracking from ineffective ones, under a dual-gate (detector-evasion + content-preservation) success criterion. On 777 UnsafeBench unsafe images, RedEdit reaches 76.2% ASR with fewer than 2 edits on average while retaining 93.0% malicious semantics, transfers across 12 detectors without re-optimization, and exposes architecture-agnostic systemic blind spots in current image content moderation.

title: Culturally-Adapted Red-Teaming Across East and Southeast Asian Contexts: A Methodological and Comparative Analysis
abstract: This study shows that direct-translation (DT) of English safety benchmarks systematically underestimates multilingual LLM risk because it strips the cultural context embedded in threat scenarios, social norms and legal frameworks. Using a culturally-adaptive red-teaming benchmark generator extended to Korean/Japanese/Thai/Khmer (500 DT + 500 culturally-adapted CA prompts per language, 12 risk categories, 1:1 seed matching), the authors show CA yields positive delta-ASR across all 16 language x model combinations (mean +9.3 pp) and DT underestimates risk in 44 of 48 category x language combinations. A 3-criteria Cultural Realism rubric finds DT Cultural-Depth scores stay below 1.0/3.0 (mean 0.17) vs CA up to 2.51, showing DT prompts diverge from real multicultural inputs.

title: Nous: An Attempt to Extract and Inject the Cognition Behind Prediction-Market Behavior
abstract: Nous extracts a structured eight-dimension behavioral profile from real Polymarket trading activity and injects it into LLM agents via prompts to test whether human cognitive diversity can be recovered and transferred to counter the 'cognitive monoculture' of agents built on shared foundation models (frontier-model forecasting errors correlate r~0.77). Central finding is a dissociation: extraction works partially (8/14 parameters temporally stable, ICC>=0.5; wallets identifiable above chance; 2/4 dimensions predict realized profit out-of-sample), but prompt-level injection does NOT measurably transmit the profile -- structured injection shows no significant advantage over a length-matched control and the induced diversity neither reduces ensemble error correlation nor improves Brier score, locating the bottleneck in the structure-to-narrative translator before the model.

title: JailbreakOPT: Tool-Assisted Iterative Jailbreak Prompt Optimization
org: UC Davis; Renmin University of China; Nankai University; Cornell University; CUHK Shenzhen
abstract: JailbreakOPT is a tool-assisted framework for iterative single-turn jailbreak prompt optimization. It organizes diverse atomic jailbreak prompts into an attack tool library and composes them through a unified intra-episode orchestrator-mutator-evaluator-selector optimization abstraction (encode/decode chains) to generate stronger standalone attack prompts, and frames inter-episode tool selection as a contextual bandit solved with contextual Thompson sampling to reuse experience across attack episodes. Across multiple target LLMs and attack goals it improves ASR while reducing the number of attacks until success (No.A) versus atomic single-turn attacks and existing iterative single-turn optimization baselines.

title: SoK: Reconstruction Attacks on Synthetic Tabular Data (Insights from Winning the NIST CRC)
org: University of Washington Tacoma; Ghent University
abstract: First systematization of reconstruction (attribute inference) attacks on de-identified and synthetic tabular data. Contributes a taxonomy organizing attacks by exploited structure, evaluates 14 attacks against 9 SDG methods across 5 benchmark datasets (the strongest, CoBP-RA, is new), and a memorization test that distinguishes reconstruction of population distribution from memorization of training records. Findings: SDG method choice governs risk more than attack choice; differential privacy protects mainly at small budgets (epsilon<=1) then plateaus; de-identification is the most exposed family; most reconstruction reflects distributional structure not memorization, concentrating individual risk on atypical records. Externally validated by first-place finish among red teams in the 2025 NIST Collaborative Research Cycle.

title: No Hidden Prompts Needed! You Can Game AI Peer Review with Presentation-Only Revisions
abstract: Studies a policy-relevant failure mode of AI peer review with no hidden text, no prompt injection, and no changes to methods/experiments/figures/equations/proofs/numerical results — the attacker modifies only presentation-level content (abstract, contribution framing, related work, discussion, narrative). Introduces adversarial repackaging: a closed-loop attack using AI-reviewer feedback to search presentation-level revisions while holding scientific evidence fixed. Across three reviewer models achieves 75.1% attack success rate and +1.21/10 mean score gain. Reveals two structural failure modes: AI reviewers are easier to impress than to convince (strength amplification reliable, weakness rebuttal backfires 31.6%), and AI reviewers confuse the appearance of addressing a limitation with resolving it. Releases a contamination-free rolling benchmark and attack framework.

title: Does AI Reviewer See the Full Picture? Attacking and Defending Multimodal Peer Review
org: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill; Arizona State University
abstract: Introduces PaperGuard, first comprehensive benchmark to systematically evaluate and defend AI-generated peer review against domain-specific, cross-modal adversarial attacks. Three pillars: (1) a multimodal peer-review dataset (1136 papers from ICLR and F1000Research, parsed to extract text and key figures); (2) a unified attack suite — black-box prompt injection plus white-box GCG (text) and PGD/APGD/C&W (image figure perturbation) — targeting score inflation, a domain-specific targeted failure distinct from jailbreaking; (3) a chunk-based embedding-similarity-search defense for the long-context needle-in-haystack problem. Black-box prompt injection reaches up to 80% ASR against proprietary models (Claude-Sonnet-4.5) with +14.14 score inflation; white-box visual attacks inflate scores up to +14.11 via imperceptible figure perturbation alone. Chunk-based defense achieves 95.0%/93.5% text/visual accuracy at near-zero FPR and 100% recall on 17 real arxiv papers with confirmed hidden injections.

title: Domain-Conditioned Safety in Frontier Computer-Using Agents: A 793-Episode Browser Benchmark, a Coding-Domain Cross-Reference, and a Reproducibility Audit of Recent Red-Teaming
org: Patronus AI; University of California, Berkeley
abstract: Asks whether headline CUA red-teaming techniques (RL-Hammer, WASP, TRAP, RedTeamCUA, MUZZLE; reported ASR 42-98%) reproduced as hand-crafted templates still work against current frontier CUAs. Releases CUA-HANDCRAFTED, a 793-episode public benchmark (24 multi-step web tasks, 56 attack templates, 8 attack families, 4 system-prompt configs). Against Claude Sonnet 4.6 and GPT-5.4 measures 0/140 multi-step attack success (Clopper-Pearson 95% upper bound 2.60%); a prompt ablation shows resistance lives in model weights not the system prompt. Yet it does not generalize: on a sister coding-agent benchmark (SKILLBENCH) the same weights fall to hand-crafted skill-injection at up to 100%. Argues literature's high ASR is largely attributable to RL-optimized injection text, and frontier safety hardening is domain-conditioned (browser-specific). Reporting techniques without releasing optimized strings, or extrapolating browser-domain safety to other CUA modalities, makes published ASR numbers unreproducible.

title: Stateful Online Monitoring Catches Distributed Agent Attacks
org: University of Pennsylvania; Carnegie Mellon University
abstract: Builds the first distributed agent attack — a multi-agent scaffold that completes hard cybersecurity tasks while hiding the harmful objective across subagents with limited contexts, evading a standard per-transcript monitor by splitting misuse across many user accounts so each transcript looks benign; caught only a fifth as often as prior agent attacks. Develops an online stateful monitor that uses real-time clustering to collect weak suspiciousness signals across many agent transcripts and escalates rarely to a language model that flags misuse across user accounts. Pareto dominates standard monitors, catching distributed attacks 30% earlier and flagging cyber misuse before the most harmful stages, at negligible latency for ~99% of traffic. An extensive red-teaming exercise (>100k attacks, 2 months) further improves the defense and finds it also catches standard jailbreaks since adaptive attackers reuse attack variants across accounts.

title: Grammar-Constrained Decoding Can Jailbreak LLMs into Generating Malicious Code
org: Tsinghua University; University of Electronic Science and Technology of China
abstract: Reveals that Grammar-Constrained Decoding (GCD), a reliability mechanism for code generation, can be turned into an attack surface. The CodeSpear jailbreak applies a benign off-the-shelf code grammar to constrain decoding, removing the natural-language refusal from the valid output space and forcing the model to emit malicious code. No adversarial grammar, no gradient, no fine-tuning, no prompt engineering required — only a standard GCD interface. Evaluated on 10 LLMs across 4 benchmarks; the CodeShield honeypot-code DPO defense restores safety under GCD.

title: SlotGCG: Exploiting the Positional Vulnerability in LLMs for Jailbreak Attacks
abstract: Shows that GCG-family jailbreaks waste capacity by restricting adversarial tokens to a fixed suffix slot. Introduces the Vulnerable Slot Score (VSS), an attention-based metric that quantifies how susceptible each insertion position ('slot') is to adversarial tokens, and SlotGCG, which distributes adversarial tokens across high-VSS slots. The position-search mechanism is attack-agnostic and plugs into any optimization-based attack with ~200ms preprocessing, yielding +14% average ASR over GCG-based methods, faster convergence, and 42% higher ASR under input-filtering defenses. ICLR 2026.

title: MLingualFC: Evaluating Jailbreak Vulnerabilities in Multilingual Vision-Language Models
org: DJ Sanghvi College of Engineering; King's College London; IIT Jodhpur
abstract: Introduces MLingualFC, a multilingual multimodal benchmark that encodes harmful instructions as structured flowchart images (horizontal/vertical/tortuous layouts) across Hindi, Punjabi, Spanish, Romanian, and German, paired with a benign text prompt. Evaluates Qwen2.5-VL, Gemma-4, and Pangea under a black-box single-turn threat model. Visual encoding of harmful content combined with non-English text bypasses safety alignment that operates only in text and in English. Latin-script languages reach >80% ASR while Indic scripts show low ASR attributed to weak visual text recognition, not stronger safety.

title: MaskForge: Structure-Aware Adaptive Attacks for Jailbreaking Diffusion Large Language Models
org: University of Wisconsin-Madison; Johns Hopkins University; University of Southern California; RAIR Centre, University of Adelaide
abstract: Diffusion LLMs (dLLMs) generate text by iteratively denoising masked spans under bidirectional context, exposing a safety surface distinct from autoregressive LLMs: mask tokens are native inputs and harmful content can be induced through the model's own infilling rather than attacker-written continuation. MaskForge is a black-box adaptive attack that casts dLLM red-teaming as optimized search over a growing library of reusable structural patterns (typed mask-bearing scaffolds), selected via a UCB bandit with a scorer-guided drafter fallback. Achieves 79.3% avg ASR (+17.6% relative over strongest dLLM baseline) across 5 dLLMs and 3 benchmarks; the matured pattern library transfers to AdvBench at 88.2% ASR with no further updates.

title: MultiTurnPSB: Evaluating Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attacks and Classifier-Based Defenses for Medical AI Safety
abstract: Extends PatientSafetyBench (466 patient-facing medical safety prompts, 5 categories) into a four-turn adversarial dialogue benchmark with three attack modalities (fixed-template, template-adaptive, live adversarial). Evaluates GPT-4.1-mini and Claude Sonnet 4.5. Unsafe responses rise from 35% to ~80% by Turn 4 under live attack; two models statistically indistinguishable at baseline diverge to a 19x gap by Turn 4. Identifies a two-element attack formula (emergency framing + medical authority claim) responsible for most catastrophic failures, with Turn 2 the critical vulnerability window. A lightweight input-side classifier reduces Turn-4 unsafe rate by 52.2 pp but with a 45% benign false-alarm rate. Also finds Claude refused to act as adversarial attacker in >half of late-turn conversations.

title: Evaluating Privilege Usage of Agents with Real-World Tools
abstract: GrantBox is a security evaluation sandbox that automatically integrates real-world MCP servers and lets LLM agents invoke genuine privileges, enabling evaluation of privilege usage under prompt injection. Ten real-world MCP servers with 122 privilege-sensitive tools (cloud infra, databases, personal data) were integrated; 100 benign privileged requests (avg 5.67 tools) and 50 privilege-hijacking cases across five attack categories were generated. Four LLMs (GPT-5, Gemini3-Flash, Qwen3-Max, Deepseek-v3) evaluated in ReAct and Plan-and-Execute modes show average ASR 90.55% (ReAct) and 79.05% (Plan-and-Execute), reaching 84.80% average in carefully crafted scenarios. FSE Companion '26.

title: A Framework for Formalizing LLM Agent Security
org: UC Santa Cruz / UC Berkeley / Duke University
abstract: A contextual-security framework systematizing LLM agent attacks and defenses. Defines execution context C_t=(p,Tr_{t-1},M_t,E_t,S_auth,t,G) and four security properties — task alignment, action alignment, source authorization, data isolation — verified by five oracle functions (instruction attribution I, source attribution L, objective evaluators H_p/H_Tr/H_a). Reformalizes indirect/direct prompt injection, jailbreak, task drift, agentic misalignment, confused deputy, capability misuse, cross-context leakage, malicious tool exploitation, and memory poisoning as violations of one or more properties. Analysis of 87 papers maps documented attacks to property violations; existing context-agnostic defenses are structurally incapable of distinguishing attack from legitimate task.

title: Beyond Single-Agent Alignment: Preventing Context-Fragmented Violations in Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: Identifies and formalizes Context-Fragmented Violations (CFVs) — cross-agent action sequences where each agent action is locally policy-compliant but collectively violates organizational invariants because critical policy facts are siloed in different departments' private contexts. Also formalizes Semantic Laundering (loss of security taint as information flows through LLM summarization/paraphrasing). Proposes Distributed Sentinel: a sidecar zero-trust architecture with a Semantic Taint Token (STT) protocol and Counterfactual Graph Simulation. On the PhantomEcosystem benchmark (200 scenarios, 9 CFV categories), Distributed Sentinel reaches F1=0.95 vs 0.85 (prompt filtering) and 0.65 (rule-based DLP). Eight frontier LLMs (Claude Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash, GPT-5.4/-mini/-nano, GPT-4.1) show 14-98% violation rates in cross-domain multi-agent workflows.

title: Ghost in the Agent: Redefining Information Flow Tracking for LLM Agents
abstract: NeuroTaint is a provenance-oriented offline taint-tracking framework for LLM agents. Key insight: taint propagation in agents must capture not only explicit content propagation but also semantic transformation, causal influence on decisions, and cross-session persistence through memory. It identifies three orthogonal information-flow classes (explicit content propagation, implicit control influence, asynchronous provenance reuse) requiring different detection. Built on a Dynamic Context Provenance Graph (DCPG) backbone plus a Hybrid Semantic Tracker and a Sink-Driven Causal Analyzer. On TaintBench (400 scenarios, 20 frameworks) NeuroTaint reaches P=0.921/R=0.935/F1=0.928 vs F1=0.522 for FIDES (IFC baseline), while remaining effective on InjecAgent and ToolEmu.

title: The Granularity Mismatch in Agent Security: Argument-Level Provenance Solves Enforcement and Isolates the LLM Reasoning Bottleneck
org: Renmin University of China / KAUST / Dongbei University of Finance and Economics / USTC
abstract: Identifies the granularity mismatch in agent security: indirect prompt injection becomes dangerous not when untrusted content appears in context, but when it determines an AUTHORITY-BEARING ARGUMENT of a tool call. Whole-call defenses force a brittle choice (allow content to influence calls and risk hijacked destinations, or quarantine and block benign retrieve-then-act). PACT (Provenance-Aware Capability Contracts) is a runtime monitor that assigns semantic roles to tool arguments (target/command/credential/content/selector/control), tracks value provenance across replanning steps, and checks each argument against its role-specific trust requirement. Under oracle provenance PACT achieves 100% utility and 100% security on mixed-trust suites; in full AgentDojo across five models it reaches 100% security on the three strongest models while recovering 38.1-46.4% utility, 8-16 points above CaMeL.

title: Trust No Tool: Evaluating and Defending LLM Agents under Untrusted Tool Feedback
org: Southern University of Science and Technology / USTC / University of Birmingham / Zhejiang University / ECNU / Alibaba Group
abstract: Studies cognitive poisoning: a malicious tool behaves plausibly during exploration, accumulates trust through benign-looking feedback, and becomes harmful only when hidden state conditions align with the final executable action. Constructs TRUST-Bench (1,970 episodes / 1,753 source tasks, 7,012 variants from 5 upstream suites) of task-conditioned hidden-trigger tool-compromise episodes with matched safe controls, introduces the asymmetric GuardedJoint metric, and presents VISTA-Guard, a backbone-agnostic final-action risk scorer using trajectory-state and parameter evidence. Under GuardedJoint VISTA-Guard reaches 84.2 in-domain and 56.9 balanced OOD, while prompt-centric, heuristic, and scalarized baselines collapse to zero.

title: Attack Selection in Agentic AI Control Evaluations Meaningfully Decreases Safety
org: University of Oxford / MARS / CAISH / Georgia Tech / MATS / Astra / Redwood Research
abstract: Studies attack selection in agentic AI control evaluations: an attacker that strategically chooses WHEN to attack (vs indiscriminately) is much harder to catch. Decomposes attack decisions into a task-level start policy (whether a main-task/side-task pair is worth attacking) and a per-turn stop policy (whether to abort an in-progress attack). Across BashArena and LinuxArena under trusted-monitoring with a 1% audit budget, the start policy lowers empirical safety by ~20pp and the stop policy by 20-28pp, without changing underlying attack capability. Recommends control evaluations, system cards, and safety cases explicitly elicit attack selection to avoid overly optimistic safety estimates.

title: Risk Under Pressure: Compute-Aware Evaluation of Adversarial Robustness in Language Models
org: University of Toronto / Vector Institute / Hugging Face
abstract: Adversarial-robustness evaluations of LLMs typically report attack success rate (ASR) at a fixed query budget, implicitly treating all attacks as equally costly. Proposes a compute-aware evaluation framework based on computational pressure measured in cumulative FLOPs as a proxy for adversarial effort. Introduces risk-compute curves mapping compute budgets to attack risk, and two scalar metrics: C@tau (compute to reach tau% risk) and AE (average efficiency, risk per FLOP). Across ten models, four training/alignment stages, three attacks (GCG, PAIR, JailBroken) on HarmBench + JailbreakBench, finds alignment training has non-monotonic effects on compute-space robustness, scaling reduces gradient-attack effectiveness but not template attacks, surrogate-optimized attacks transfer, compute cost varies up to ~5x across harm categories, and safety-RL leaves some categories disproportionately accessible.

title: SeClaw: Spec-Driven Security Task Synthesis for Evaluating Autonomous Agents
org: HKUST / Ant Digital Technologies / Xi'an Jiaotong / Oxford / CityU HK / MIT / Zhejiang U / UNC
abstract: SeClaw is a framework combining specification-driven security task synthesis and execution-based security evaluation for autonomous LLM agents. Spec-Driven Security Task Synthesis uses a multi-agent collaborative pipeline (with Claude Code + human experts) to generate security tasks from structured risk specifications, covering resource, task, environment, and intrinsic risks. A Docker-based testbed (SeClaw-Docker) reconstructs task-specific user environments via ToolHub-based Skill and MCP configurations, logs fine-grained agent-environment trajectories, and supports trajectory-aware assessment of unsafe actions beyond final responses. Provides a reproducible foundation for measuring, diagnosing, and comparing security failures in autonomous LLM agents.

title: ARuleCon: Agentic Security Rule Conversion
org: National University of Singapore / Fudan University / NCS Group
abstract: ARuleCon is the first agentic framework for autonomous cross-SIEM security rule conversion. It distills a source rule's core detection logic into a vendor-agnostic conversion Intermediate Representation (IR), drafts the target rule via LLM reasoning, then refines it with two autonomous reflection agents: an Agentic-RAG pipeline that retrieves authoritative vendor documentation to fix convention/schema mismatches, and a Python-based consistency check that compiles source and target IRs into executable code and runs both over synthetic test logs to verify functional equivalence. Evaluated on 1,492 rule-conversion pairs across five mainstream SIEM platforms (Splunk SPL, Microsoft KQL, IBM AQL, Google YARA-L, RSA ESA), ARuleCon improves logic alignment, semantic validity, and execution success, outperforming general LLMs by ~15% in similarity. Industry case studies with Singtel Singapore.

title: Reframing LLM Agent Security as an Agent-Human Interaction Problem
abstract: Argues LLM agent security is fundamentally an agent-human interaction (AHI) problem, not a purely algorithmic one. Systematic analysis of 59 academic papers, 21 production agent systems, and 26 security plugins (as of April 2026) reveals that three human-centric security mechanisms (policy specification, runtime approval, scope configuration) dominate industry practice (adopted by 14-16 of 21 systems), while the categories most heavily studied in academia (intent anchoring and trust labeling) see ZERO production deployment. Current human-participation mechanisms suffer a cognitive-burden vs security-guarantee trade-off, leaving users caught between approval fatigue and uncontrolled agent autonomy. Proposes a three-direction research agenda and calls for AHI security to be a first-class research citizen.

title: Can Agents Secure Hardware? Evaluating Agentic LLM-Driven Obfuscation for IP Protection
org: University of Arizona / Arizona State University
abstract: Presents an agentic LLM-driven framework for automated hardware netlist obfuscation for IP protection. The framework combines retrieval-grounded planning, structured lock-plan generation, deterministic netlist compilation, functional verification, and SAT-based security evaluation, decomposing the task into specialized stages rather than single prompt-to-output generation. Evaluated on ISCAS-85 benchmarks with functional equivalence checking and SAT-based attacks across GPT-5, LLaMA-3.1-8B, and Qwen-2.5-Coder-14B (72 runs). Results show the framework generates correct locked netlists with measurable wrong-key output corruption, but SAT attacks remain effective in all cases, highlighting both the potential and current limitations of agentic LLM-driven obfuscation.

title: OCELOT: Inference-Leakage Budgets for Privacy-Preserving LLM Agents
abstract: LLM agents act on a user's behalf, leaking PII across trust boundaries at every step. Privacy is a property of an entire trajectory; leakage is cumulative across honest-but-curious or colluding sinks, bidirectional (observations can inject instructions), and task-dependent. The paper recasts agent privacy as posterior-risk control and presents OCELOT, a runtime mediator that budgets how much an adversary's belief about a secret may improve across a trajectory. Its mechanism, Witness-Verified Declassification (WVD), separates judgment from trust: an untrusted locally fine-tuned defender LLM inspects each candidate release and emits structured evidence; a deterministic trusted verifier audits it, charges a certified min-entropy cost, and authorizes the least-disclosing variant under a sink-trust-weighted budget on a tamper-evident ledger. Across five benchmarks and five defenses, OCELOT attains lowest leakage at higher task utility, resists adaptive injection, jailbreak, cumulative inference, and sink collusion, at 18% overhead.

title: Learning of Robot Safety Policies via Adversarial Synthetic Scenarios
abstract: Ensuring safety of robotic systems in open-ended human-centric environments is a fundamental challenge. Foundation-model robots generalize via in-context learning and fine-tuning but lack systematic mechanisms for structured safety knowledge, while hazard-informed engineering pipelines suffer combinatorial explosion at scale. The paper proposes an agentic gamification framework: scenario generation is an adversarial game between a Red Team agent that constructs hazardous situations and a Blue Team agent that incrementally refines safety policies. A five-stage hazard-informed pipeline (asset declaration, exposure modeling, hazard scenario definition, simulation-based data generation, safety-oriented training) is formalized. A proof-of-concept Webots experiment trains a safe/unsafe object-placement classifier.

title: SafeMed-R1: Clinician-Audited Safety and Ethics Alignment for Medical Large Language Models
abstract: Medical LLMs match expert performance on licensing exams yet routine clinical use is limited because governance requires auditable reasoning, safety/ethics alignment, and resilience to adversarial misuse. SafeMed-R1 is trained with a traceable Clinical Trust Signals (CTS) pipeline linking each reasoning instance to clinician rubric scores and edit histories, and aligned via safety/ethics supervision and red-team stress testing. It attains 79.6% macro-averaged accuracy across clinical benchmarks; under adversarial safety testing it shows the lowest aggregated risk and reduces unsafe outputs by about 3-5% relative to its baseline. In a paired expert study of 30 medication-safety vignettes it matches PGY1/PGY2 residents on correctness and scores higher for medication safety, guideline consistency, and clinical usefulness.

title: AI Scientists Are Only as Good as Their Evidence: A Stratified Ablation of Proprietary Data and Reasoning Skills in Drug-Asset Valuation
abstract: AI Scientist agents are often evaluated as if capability were mainly a function of model quality, prompting, or reasoning scaffolds. In specialized scientific/commercial domains the limiting factor may be the evidence substrate: the private, curated, long-tail record on which the agent reasons. A controlled three-arm ablation on a production drug-asset valuation agent — A (plain LLM + web search), B (+ public structured tools, verifier, objectivity policy, adversarial red-team), and C (+ proprietary Noah AI database) — run on Claude Code with Opus 4.8 MAX. Skills/public tools improve calibration (tier-in-range 0.80->0.89) and objectivity (3.16->3.30) but do not remove the factual ceiling: A and B recover only 0.25 and 0.38 of the curated gold competitive record while C recovers 0.96. Completeness-aware informed decision-quality is 7.43 for C vs 1.76/2.57 for A/B.

title: Understanding Safety-Sensitive Expert Behavior in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
org: Huazhong University of Science and Technology; Nanyang Technological University
abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs rely on sparse router-driven expert activation, yet how safety alignment interacts with routed expert specialization is underexplored. Through three routing probes the paper provides evidence that routing in aligned MoE LLMs is largely topic-driven while safety behavior can be altered with little change to the intrinsic routing path: safety-related refusal is mediated inside expert representations rather than by router-selected safety routes. Motivated by this, it presents RASET (Router-Agnostic Safety-critical Expert Tuning), a red-teaming framework that identifies safety-critical experts via a contrastive routing-sensitivity criterion and applies parameter-efficient tuning only to selected experts, reaching 50.5% average ASR_hq while updating only 0.12-0.95% of parameters and preserving benign utility.

title: Aligning Provenance with Authorization: A Dual-Graph Defense for LLM Agents
abstract: LLM agents interact with the external world through tool calling and must read external data sources attackers can control; through indirect prompt injection attackers embed malicious instructions to manipulate agents into unauthorized operations. Existing defenses perform tool-call-level value checking without tracking where parameter values originate, or analyze execution traces from a single perspective without a clean authorization baseline. AUTHGRAPH constructs two complementary graphs: an injected reasoning graph (IRG) modeling provenance from the actual trajectory (including manipulated attributions), and an authorization graph (AG) derived from user intent in an isolated clean context that is information-theoretically impossible to influence by injection; a graph alignment checker structurally compares them to detect tool-level and parameter-source-level deviations. On AgentDojo it reduces ASR 40%->1% (UR 76%) on GPT-4o; on AgentDyn 39%->2% (UR 51%).

title: Black-box, Adaptive, Efficient, Transferable, Harmful, Applicable... Attacks Are All You Need to Break LLMs
org: Technical University of Munich / Munich Data Science Institute / Helmholtz AI
abstract: Introduces Indirect Harm Optimization (IHO), a masked diffusion language model attacker trained via iterative Direct Preference Optimization against an LLM harmfulness judge, requiring only black-box access to the target. The same method serves as a strong adaptive attack on individual behaviors, or as an efficient amortized policy that transfers to held-out behaviors and unseen target models without fine-tuning. Against layered defenses (Circuit Breaker + auxiliary detector), IHO improves attack success considerably over SOTA without defense-specific adaptation. Proposes Expected Volume Under the Surface (EVUS) as a more reliable metric than ASR.

title: Learning to Attack and Defend: Adaptive Red Teaming of Language Models via GRPO
org: Microsoft AI Red Team / Microsoft Azure
abstract: Introduces AdvGRPO, an attacker-defender co-training framework that makes GRPO viable for joint optimization using dense multi-channel rewards (attack, prompt, thinking-trace, helpfulness) and Group reward-Decoupled Policy Optimization (GDPO) advantage normalization, plus a curriculum from single-turn to closed-loop multi-turn attacks. Produces highly effective and transferable single-turn, multi-turn, and reasoning attackers, and co-trained defenders that outperform baselines on safety benchmarks while preserving utility. Shows unaligned models do not automatically make good attackers.

title: Agentic AI and the Industrialization of Cyber Offense: Forecast, Consequences, and Defensive Priorities for Enterprises and the Mittelstand
abstract: A bounded evidence synthesis arguing that agentic AI is an attack compression technology: it lowers the time, skill, and cost to move through intrusion phases (reconnaissance, phishing, credential abuse, vulnerability triage, exploit adaptation, post-compromise decision support). Introduces a Three-Channel Agentic Cyber-Risk Model (attacker-side augmentation, agentic systems as targets, internal agents as risky actors) and an Agentic Attack Compression Model. Uses the 2026 Linux kernel Copy Fail incident (CVE-2026-31431) as a foothold-to-root case study and develops a 2026-2028 forecast and prioritized defense roadmap.

title: Towards Optimal Agentic Architectures for Offensive Security Tasks
abstract: A controlled 600-run benchmark of 20 interactive offensive-security targets (10 web/API, 10 binary), each exposing one ground-truth vulnerability, evaluated across five agent coordination topologies (SAS, MAS-Indep, MAS-Decent, MAS-Central, MAS-Hybrid), three model families (GPT-5.2, Claude Opus 4, Kimi K2), and whitebox/blackbox access modes. Detection-any reaches 58.0% and validated detection 49.8%. MAS-Indep attains the highest validated detection (64.2%); SAS is the strongest efficiency baseline at $0.058 per validated finding. Whitebox materially outperforms blackbox (67.0% vs 32.7%) and web outperforms binary (74.3% vs 25.3%). The main result is a non-monotonic cost-quality frontier: broader coordination does not dominate once latency, token cost, and exploit-validation difficulty are considered.

title: Security Attack and Defense Strategies for Autonomous Agent Frameworks: A Layered Review with OpenClaw as a Case Study
org: Nantong University / State Key Lab for Novel Software Technology, Nanjing University
abstract: A layered review of security risks and defenses in autonomous agent frameworks organized into four security-relevant layers: context/instruction, tool/action, state/persistence, and ecosystem/automation. For each layer it summarizes the attack surface, representative attacks, and defenses, then identifies cross-layer threat propagation where a single injected instruction escalates from manipulated input to unsafe action to persistent state contamination to ecosystem-level impact. Uses the OpenClaw framework as a case study and highlights research imbalance across layers, lack of long-horizon evaluation, and weak ecosystem trust models.

title: Smarter Saboteurs, Better Fixers: Scaling & Security in Linear Multi-Agent Workflows
abstract: Investigates how model scale affects the security of strictly linear LLM-based multi-agent SDLC workflows by injecting an adversarially-instructed 'Mischievous Engineer' agent that introduces subtle logic bugs into generated code, evaluated on HumanEval across five parameter sizes of Gemma 3 and Qwen 3.5. Reveals a compliance-correction symmetry: larger models are far more likely to faithfully execute malicious instructions (uncorrected malicious drop reaching 53.7pp at 27B), but a lightweight terminal QA->Fixer correction stage collapses this to 0.6pp, restoring statistical parity. The brittleness attributed to linear topology may stem from lack of correction rather than topology itself.

title: Towards Security-Auditable LLM Agents: A Unified Graph Representation
org: Huazhong University of Science and Technology / Nanyang Technological University / Fudan University
abstract: Proposes Agent-BOM (Agent Bill of Materials), a unified hierarchical attributed directed graph for security auditing of LLM agentic systems. It separates a static capability layer (models, prompts, tools, skills, long-term memory, code) from a runtime semantic layer (goals, context, reasoning, decisions, actions, observations), connected by structural-dependency, runtime-evolution, cross-layer-binding, and cross-agent-propagation edges with security attributes. A 4-tuple auditing rule (entry localization, backward tracing, forward tracing, adjudication conditions) maps the OWASP Agentic Top 10 to queryable audit paths. Instantiated on OpenClaw (GPT-5 base) and evaluated on four composite attack scenarios covering all ten ASI risks.

title: Self-Adaptive Multi-Agent LLM-Based Security Pattern Selection for IoT Systems
abstract: Introduces ASPO, a self-adaptive multi-agent LLM-based runtime security pattern selection system for resource-constrained IoT edge gateways. ASPO integrates LLM-based reasoning with deterministic enforcement inside a MAPE-K control loop, explicitly separating stochastic decision generation (LLM agents proposing candidate mitigation portfolios) from deterministic execution (a closed-world optimization core enforcing action integrity, conflict-free composition, and resource feasibility). Five specialized agents (Context, Reasoner, Constraint, Planner, Audit) propose candidates over a closed catalogue of 10 security patterns; only a deterministic validation layer actuates. Evaluated on a distributed edge testbed (10 Raspberry Pi 4) with the Bot-IoT dataset over 500/1000 decisions, achieving 100% conflict-free activation, perfect rank preservation, and 21.9%/23.1% tail latency/energy reduction.

title: Alignment Contracts for Agentic Security Systems
abstract: Introduces alignment contracts, a formal framework for specifying and enforcing behavioral constraints over observable effect traces of offensive-capable agentic security systems (e.g., autonomous pentest agents). A contract C=<S,E_allow,E_forbid,B,D,Res,cost,flows> defines scope, allowed/forbidden effects, resource budgets, and disclosure sinks. The paper gives finite-trace-based semantics, characterizes satisfaction as a safety property with finite violation witnesses, develops refinement and one-way composition, and proves admissibility checking is decidable. Under an Effect Observability Assumption (EOA), a reference monitor produces only contract-satisfying traces regardless of the underlying model (Enforcement Soundness, Theorem 6.5), including adversarial/prompt-injected agents. Establishes impossibility results (pre-admission forbidden-effect absence is undecidable; mediation-bypassing tools void soundness). A Lean 4 artifact mechanizes the core theorems.

title: SafeAgent: A Runtime Protection Architecture for Agentic Systems
org: Lomonosov Moscow State University / Central University
